title: FairShare on-call simulator and escalation load balancer
author: Maya Bennett
release_notes: Adds a FairShare simulator and a policy-driven escalation load balancer to help teams evaluate on-call fairness, page routing, and noisy-signal dampening. Includes a lightweight CLI and telemetry exporter for dashboarding.
description:
Background and motivation: on-call teams at Redwood have been asking for a way to quantify how routing policy changes affect responder load, mean-time-to-ack, and user-visible SLOs. This PR introduces a deterministic, configurable "FairShare" simulator plus an in-service escalation load balancer that can be enabled behind a feature flag. Goals: 1) let platform teams run synthetic experiments (shift patterns, incident types, noisy alerts) and get per-actor load and fairness metrics; 2) provide runtime fallback routing that respects capacity and recent load to avoid overloading responders; 3) reduce alert thrash by dampening noisy signals before escalation.

What this contains (single-string description): Implementation summary: FairShare simulator (pkg/sim/fairshare) with a scenario DSL, synthetic alert generators (rate/jitter/severity models), responder effectiveness models (ack latency distribution, routing failure), and a metrics exporter. Escalation load balancer (pkg/escalation/lb) implements token-bucket capacity windows per-responder, short-term heat scores, and a configurable fairness function (minimize max-load, weighted round-robin, recency-penalty). A new CLI command (tools/oncall-sim) runs batch experiments and outputs CSV/JSON summaries. A lightweight Prometheus exporter (observability/oncall_exporter.go) publishes: responder_load, simulated_ack_latency_histogram, fairness_index, dampened_alert_rate. Feature flagging: runtime toggle via /config/feature_flags.yaml and a env var REDWOOD_ONCALL_LB=true. Tests: unit tests for fairness scoring, integration test harness that runs small synthetic scenarios, and a smoke test that boots the load balancer with a mocked responder pool. Backwards compatibility: load balancer is opt-in behind feature flag; fallback is current round-robin routing. Migration plan: ship as opt-in to a few internal teams, collect telemetry for two weeks, iterate on fairness function defaults. Checklist: - [x] Simulator code + DSL - [x] Escalation LB core logic - [x] CLI + exporter - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Docs: docs/oncall/fairshare.md - [x] Feature flag gating - [x] Benchmarks (micro-bench for fairness calc) Usage notes: The CLI supports scenario templates in YAML and a --replay-mode to feed historical alert streams. The LB supports max_concurrent and heat_half_life config knobs. See docs/oncall/fairshare.md for sample policies and recommended thresholds. Related: ENG-9021 (oncall fairness study), SUP-4127 (support case where one responder overloads in p99 incidents).

notes_for_ops: Feature is gated. Helm values: incidentBot.oncallLoadBalancer.enabled=false by default. To enable for a team: set incidentBot.oncallLoadBalancer.enabled=true and configure incidentBot.oncallLoadBalancer.policy with a policy id from docs. Collect the following metrics for 2 weeks: oncall_responder_load, fairness_index, dampened_alert_rate, simulated_ack_latency_histogram.
